correction.reason: The original issue applied R60 internal blueprint cleanup wording to every final control handle as if it were a separate user requirement. D11 P5-03/Q13 requires safe actual maintenance, data preservation and qualified upgrade/uninstall; it does not require an unending negative marker after all maintenance producers have physically returned merely because the last control-handle close reported failure. The prior report is retained unchanged for evidence; this correction supersedes its P1 user-risk conclusion.
correction.stillTrueSourceObservation: SetDisposition and Pending close precede Parent/Gate closes. A failed close retains raw handles and faults the process; delete-pending may complete when the process exits. This describes control lifetime only after the required settlement/physical-producer fence, not an unknown installer transaction automatically treated as settled.

beforeNegativeDelete: Original operation/deadline and Pending inode/ACL/readback still verified under the retained exclusive original gate and directory pins.
Trusted Join0/End0 plus effects reconciliation, original guardian process object signaled with exit0; no mere receipt, timeout, missing PID or unknown rollback may substitute.

All non-control native resources/producer capabilities physically returned with checked closes. In this narrow core these are Guardian/Token handles; external broker future integration must account for its own IPC, workers, callbacks and descendants before effects_reconciled.
Any pre-settlement failure, live guardian or failing ancillary close keeps Pending and original physical gate.
afterNegativeDelete: Only coordination Pending/Parent/Gate control handles may remain. Keep handle-based deletion and original parent/gate pins; do not replace with final DeleteFileW on an unpinned path.
Any failed native close is sticky in the current process, retains the remaining original handle capabilities and never returns Released or opens a replacement owner.

If that original process later physically exits, OS return of its original gate becomes the final kernel fence. A later startup must actually acquire the same validated physical share gate and observe no Pending before continuing. There are no unreturned maintenance producers at that point.
executableSafetyBoundary.originalImplementationAssessment: Original clear_pending already closes every non-Parent/Gate/Pending role before deleting Pending; after the settlement/actual-exit checks, remaining native roles are control-only. No path-CAS or infinite sentinel protocol is required for the clarified user invariant.
executableSafetyBoundary.claimLimit: This is source/control-flow reasoning, not actual Windows close-failure/runtime proof or complete MSI-owner integration.
